chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the one who is fearful (of missing the prescribed times), there is no problem if he were to pelt the Jamarat at night, and sacrifice (the animal) at night, and depart (from Mina) at night.

key_terms.الْخَائِف: The one who is fearful (of missing ritual times)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim perform Hajj rituals at night if they are afraid of missing the time?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility of Hajj rituals for the 'khaif' (one fearing harm or missing the window), explicitly permitting the stoning of the Jamarat, sacrifice (dhabh), and departure from Mina (ifad) at night. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling alleviates the burden on pilgrims who, due to fear or necessity, cannot perform these acts during the prescribed daytime hours, ensuring the validity of their Hajj without penalty. It underscores the principle of ease (taysir) in ritual obligations when specific conditions of fear or forgetfulness apply.
